pull.title: test: Add test for CompactSize larger than MAX_SIZE value
pull.body:
Currently there is no test coverage for oversized CompactSize. This is fine, because a vector this large will already be rejected earlier by the P2P transport payload size check.

However, it would be good to still add test coverage:

* Removing the check would pass all tests.
* There is some accidental non-deterministic coverage through tx-deser "fuzzing", which hurts coverage reports, see https://github.com/corecheck/corecheck/pull/219#discussion_r4554170963.
* Having explicit end-to-end P2P coverage for such corrupt messages seems fine.

Quite nuanced to track down! Fixing this will help with coverage determinism.

Concept ACK

If this is useful to anyone, here a script that reproduces the non-determinism in coverage. With this PR applied it is fixed.

<details>
<summary>Script</summary>

```shell
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Coverage check for the src/serialize.h "ReadCompactSize(): size too large" guard.
# Builds with LLVM coverage, then runs the unit suite's serialisation cases and one
# functional test per run, and reports the guard's execution count for each run.
# Run from the bitcoin checkout root. Needs clang, cmake, python3, llvm-profdata and
# llvm-cov on PATH. Usage: ./guard-flip.sh [runs]      (default 8)
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
RUNS=${1:-8}

echo 'Building bitcoin with coverage'

cmake -B build -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ \
  -DAPPEND_CFLAGS="-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping" \
  -DAPPEND_CXXFLAGS="-fprofile-instr-generate -fcoverage-mapping" \
  -DAPPEND_LDFLAGS="-fprofile-instr-generate" \
  -DBUILD_GUI=OFF -DBUILD_BENCH=OFF -DBUILD_FUZZ_BINARY=OFF >/dev/null
cmake --build build -j"$(nproc)" --target bitcoind bitcoin-cli test_bitcoin >/dev/null

L=$(grep -n 'ReadCompactSize(): size too large' src/serialize.h | cut -d: -f1)
echo "guard line: src/serialize.h:$L"
counts=()
for i in $(seq "$RUNS"); do
  d=$(mktemp -d)
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=$d/u_%m_%p.profraw ./build/bin/test_bitcoin --run_test=serialize_tests >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  LLVM_PROFILE_FILE=$d/f_%m_%p.profraw TMPDIR=/tmp \
    python3 build/test/functional/test_runner.py wallet_create_tx.py --randomseed=1234 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  llvm-profdata merge -o "$d/p.profdata" "$d"/*.profraw 2>/dev/null
  llvm-cov export --format=lcov --object=build/bin/bitcoind --object=build/bin/test_bitcoin \
    --instr-profile="$d/p.profdata" > "$d/info" 2>"$d/err" || true
  c=$(awk -F'[:,]' -v l="$L" '/^SF:.*serialize\.h$/ {s=1} s && $1=="DA" && $2==l {print $3; exit}' "$d/info")
  [ -n "$c" ] || { echo "run $i: no DA record for line $L, see $d/err" >&2; exit 2; }
  counts+=("$c")
  echo "run $i: $c"
  rm -rf "$d"
done
echo "counts: ${counts[*]}"
if printf '%s\n' "${counts[@]}" | grep -qx 0; then
  echo "FLIPS: the guard was left uncovered on at least one run"
else
  echo "NO FLIPS: the guard was covered on every run"
fi

```
</details>

> If this is useful to anyone, here a script that reproduces the non-determinism in coverage.

An alternative would be to just replace the code with `assert(false)` and then run the functional tests. Sometimes they pass, sometimes they fail.

events.message: test: Add P2P test for CompactSize > MAX_SIZE

comments.body: Is there a reason you opted for a generic lambda here and not a parameter called RangeCheck? More for my understanding than a nit.
This just checks 5 byte values and I did consider if we should also check 9 byte values but I don't think it really adds anything.

comments.diff_hunk:
@@ -153,6 +156,18 @@ def test_size(self):
             conn.wait_for_disconnect(timeout=1)
         self.nodes[0].disconnect_p2ps()
 
+    def test_corrupt_compactsize(self):
+        self.log.info("Test message with a vector length exceeding MAX_SIZE")
+        conn = self.nodes[0].add_p2p_connection(P2PInterface())
+        # Any vector with this many entries exceeds the P2P payload limit,
+        # so this CompactSize value is only possible in a corrupt payload.
+        msg = msg_unrecognized(str_data="")
+        msg.msgtype = b'inv'
+        msg.serialize = lambda: ser_compact_size(MAX_SIZE + 1)
+        with self.nodes[0].assert_debug_log(["ReadCompactSize(): size too large"]):
+            conn.send_and_ping(msg)
comments.body: In this situation it looks like the node will log the error but won't do any `Misbehaving` behaviour or anything. Do we think this is correct? It's just a malformed message I guess and not necessarily a large message.

comments.body:
It is impossible to enumerate all cases of "misbehavior" and it can also be net-split risky to mark something as misbehavior when ancient (pre-bip) protocol may have allowed it.

The p2p protocol message size limit was added in ba04c4a7801e7d68a5e84035b919e5c3626eb7a7 without a bip, so making MAX_SIZE+1  compactsize a misbehavior may be controversial and difficult to review. 

In any case, this is a test-only pull, so I am not allowed to change misbehavior here. Also, to give more examples, https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906 goes the opposite way and changes a bad-txns-oversize from misbehavior to an ignored deser error.

To also give an example where a new misbehavior is added based on a bip text: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35550
